body:
# Independent audit: four monotone triangle fibers

**PASS**, after the author added the requested explicit absolute-depth
convention. I independently checked every equation and all cap regimes
in candidate 680d45e380747dc3 and reran its
exact verifier. There is no mathematical repair.

The result is \(A_\mu(y)\ge (4/9)M/2\), equivalently normalized depth
at least \(2/9\). It applies to the stated positive monotone concave
four-fiber profiles, not to a profile with an interior peak.

## 1. Exact normal envelope

For a triangle \(rT\), symmetry permits \(w=(\alpha,1-\alpha)\),
\(\alpha\in[1/2,1]\). In the lower-threshold regime the cap fraction
\(1-\theta^2/[\alpha(1-\alpha)]\) decreases toward its interface.
In the upper-threshold regime the derivative of
\((\alpha-\theta)^2/[\alpha(2\alpha-1)]\) has the sign of
\(\alpha(4\theta-1)-\theta\).
Thus the coordinate normal minimizes for \(\theta\le1/3\); for
\(1/3\le\theta<1/2\) the minimizer is
\(\alpha=\theta/(4\theta-1)\).
The latter belongs to \([1-\theta,1]\), since its difference from
\(1-\theta\) is \((2\theta-1)^2/(4\theta-1)\).

This verifies the complete envelope, including zero thresholds,
supporting zero-area caps, the repeated normal, and both interfaces.
The factor \(V=|T|\) is retained consistently: the envelope is cap
volume divided by \(V\), not divided by the varying fiber volume.

## 2. Both scalar inequalities

The source's minimization in \(b\) is correct. In the middle regime,
\(P_b(x)-4b^2/9\) is concave in \(b\); at \(b=3x\) it is zero.
The two displayed factorizations for the remaining endpoint values
have the stated signs.

Here is a separate check by minimizing in \(x\). Set
\[
 F_b(x)=P_b(x)+P_1(2/3-x)-4b^2/9.
\]
For fixed \(b\in[1/2,1]\), this is concave on the interval before
\(x=b/2\): its two quadratic pieces meet with equal derivatives at
\(x=b/3\). After \(b/2\) it is again concave. Therefore only
\(x=1/6\), \(x=1/3\), and the interior junction \(x=b/2\) need be
checked. Their values or lower bounds are respectively
\[
 \frac{(2b-1)(10b-1)}{36},\qquad
 \frac49(1-b^2),\qquad
 \frac{2(1-b)(11b-4)}9 .
\]
The last junction occurs only for \(b\le2/3\). All expressions are
nonnegative on their required domains. This independently proves the
all-real two-threshold inequality.

For fixed \(t\in[1/3,1/2]\), all radii \(r\ge1\) satisfy \(t\le r/2\).
The radius derivative is \(4t\ge4r/3\) on \(2t\le r\le3t\), and
\(2(r-t)\ge4r/3\) on \(r\ge3t\). Continuity at \(r=3t\) justifies
integration across the interface and proves
\[
 P_R(t)-P_1(t)\ge\frac23(R^2-1).
\]
The source's further weakening to \((\Gamma/2)(R^2-1)\) is valid.
Its use of the letter \(d\) for \(R\) is explicitly identified as a
radius rather than the continuous dimension.

## 3. Every shared tilt

In the nonheavy case, scaling by the positive penultimate radius
gives \((a,b,1,R)\), with \(a\le b\le1\le R\),
\(R^2<a^2+b^2+1\), and \(b\ge1/2\). The last inequality follows
from concavity \(2b\ge a+1\).
The thresholds at the penultimate centroid are exactly
\[
 1/3+2\beta,\quad 1/3+\beta,\quad 1/3,\quad 1/3-\beta.
\]

- For \(\beta\ge0\), the own and last fibers pay
  \(\Gamma(1+R^2)\), sufficient because \(a^2+b^2\le1+R^2\).
- For \(\beta\le-1/6\), the first fiber is fully captured and the
  second threshold is at most \(b/3\). The stated payment
  \(a^2+\Gamma b^2+\Gamma\) reaches the target by the nonheavy
  inequality. A zero threshold really captures the full closed
  triangle; its boundary convention causes no loss.
- For \(-1/6\le\beta\le0\), the scalar inequality and radius growth
  pay \((\Gamma/2)(1+2b^2+R^2)\), which reaches the target since
  \(a\le b\). Discarding the first fiber's contribution here is a
  legitimate nonnegative lower bound.

The ranges overlap at their endpoints and exhaust the real line.
The heavy alternative includes equality and is settled by its own
ordinary triangle centroid against every ambient cap.

## 4. All original halfspaces and actual geometry

I rechecked the used portion of
common-vertex-simplex-positive-normal-reduction.md. At an own
centroid, the fiberwise barycentric swap fixes that point; the
touching affine radius majorant supplies one genuine replacement
ambient halfspace with no larger mass on any individual fiber.
It retains one common base tilt. Concavity supplies that majorant
here. For a purely base-normal closed cap, a sufficiently large
finite positive-normal tilt preserves strict-sign fibers and only
cuts down the originally whole boundary fibers. Thus no vertical
boundary fiber is treated as null.

After this exact reduction, independently minimizing the continuous
normal on each fiber only lowers the cap cost. The proof uses that
sum as a lower bound for each shared tilt; it never asserts that the
independent minimizers are realizable by one common normal.

The concave piecewise-affine radius roof defines the displayed full
convex body and realizes exactly its four integer fibers. Common
continuous scaling, an invertible continuous linear map, an affine
common-vertex shear, and reversal of the integer base have the stated
measure and membership effects. Repeated radii and zero successive
differences are covered. Zero radii and nonmonotone profiles are not
silently added to the stated theorem.

## 5. Exact verification

Reran successfully:

    python3 supporting computation verify_four_monotone_triangle_centroids.py

The output reports 169 scalar checks, 4212 cap-envelope checks,
343 growth checks, and 420 monotone concave profiles, including
exact all-tilt envelope minima for 324 nonheavy profiles.
The tilt-minimization verifier includes every envelope breakpoint,
the constant outer tails, and each interior minimum of a convex
quadratic cell. The theorem for all real parameters follows from
the proof above, not from these finite samples.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
